items.title: Balestriero and LeCun prove a Platonic Representation Theorem for JEPAs
items.summary: New arXiv paper (2610.39302, submitted Oct 29) proves that JEPAs trained separately on different modalities learn the same representation up to one rotation when trained on two views of one scene, and argues next-token prediction is a JEPA with poor views. They report 42x fewer training samples than next-token prediction to reach the same image-text alignment, and a 109M text JEPA aligning with DINOv2 and CLIP image encoders better than every LLM they tested up to 72B.

doubt.pushback: Authors' own experiments; aggregator post (alphaXiv), primary arXiv abstract read and matches. Not yet reproduced by others.

items.title: Hugging Face releases FineDNA, a 300B-token DNA plus text training set
items.summary: HuggingFaceBio published FineDNA: over 300B tokens of genomic sequences, papers and web pages mixing DNA and text, plus 200k SFT and 98k RL samples. They say midtraining Qwen3-14B on it gives the strongest open DNA model. The dataset is live on the Hub (created Oct 30).

doubt.pushback: Dataset exists; the 'strongest open model' claim is self-reported.

items.title: Karpathy builds HackerTube with Claude Opus 5.5 in about two hours
items.summary: Karpathy built hackertube.org, a YouTube-style site of 6,454 videos recommended in about 40K Hacker News comments since 2007 across 150 topics, in roughly two hours with Opus 5.5 on medium effort. By his count over 90% of tokens went to Sonnet labeling comments, and the app plus deploy took about 1M Opus tokens. Launched Oct 31 and missed by earlier sweeps; caught via recaps (no repo linked).

doubt.pushback: Build time and token split are his own estimates; the blog URL returned Not found to a plain fetch this run, site link circulates widely.

items.title: FloodDiffusion 2: open streaming 3D motion generation at 2.3 ms per step
items.summary: AlayaLab released FloodDiffusion 2, path-controllable streaming 3D human motion generation they clock at 2.3 ms per step on an RTX 4090, with paper, MIT-licensed code, models and a live HF demo.

doubt.pushback: Speed figure is self-reported; very low reach so far.
